brief: Goldman IG credit desk (Jeffrey Papai) argues spreads have barely moved through a bond rout, rate vol and the first Fed hike (1bp wider since mid-August vs 27bps/15bps in 2015/16 and 2022) because the AI capex debt machine is paused: no $3bn+ AI bond deal since September, the first such 2-month gap since the buildout began. He reads the calm as a 1-2 month buying opportunity given zero Q4 net supply and seasonals, explicitly until 2027 AI supply returns. Meanwhile AI-linked credit (Oracle, Broadcom, Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta, Nvidia, AMD, SpaceX) already trades wider than the ex-AI index while growing past 6% of index value, and Broadcom and Oracle 5-year CDS hit record wides. About $150bn of new chip financing (Broadcom/Anthropic, Broadcom/OpenAI, SpaceX/Nvidia, Amazon/Nvidia, Oracle/Nvidia) is queued, pushing 2027 front-end AI issuance toward 20-25% of short-dated IG supply and crowding out non-AI borrowers, flattening credit curves. Papai's favored trade is GSIB bank paper into earnings; the author argues dip-buyers should sell into the Q4 rally, not after it.
